references.text: God creates man in his image; the overarching creation account that 2:7 elaborates on with details about how Adam was formed.
'You are dust, and to dust you shall return' – points directly back to the fact that man was formed from the dust of the ground.
Refers to the creation of man, Adam, and emphasizes humanity's origin from God.
'The Spirit of God has made me, the breath of the Almighty gives me life' – a direct parallel to God breathing the breath of life into Adam.
The dust returns to the earth, and the spirit returns to God who gave it – linking together the dust and the breath of life from Genesis 2:7.
Man as clay in the Creator's hand – a parallel to God forming Adam from the dust of the ground.
The genealogy that ends with 'Adam, son of God' points to humanity's origin directly from God.
Paul quotes Genesis 2:7 directly: 'The first man, Adam, became a living soul' – and compares him with the last Adam, Christ, who is a life-giving spirit.
Confirms that God is the only source of life and spirit, from creation to the renewal of the people.
Complementary creation accounts that together complete the picture of man as the image of God and a living soul.
Paul uses the creation of Adam from dust as a theological contrast to Christ's heavenly origin.
A direct quote establishing a theological contrast between Adam's life as a soul and Christ's life as spirit.
